clue.text: Signals we hear from Jersey

parts.note: Jersey looks like the island or a sweater, but it is a breed of dairy cow, and the signals heard from such an animal are the bells hung round its neck

explanation.surface: A radio enthusiast picks up transmissions from the Channel Islands.
explanation.walkthrough: A Jersey is a breed of dairy cow named after the Channel Island; the bells farmers hang on cows let you hear where they are.
explanation.definitionFit: Bells hung on grazing cattle sound out their position, so they act as audible signals from the herd.

clue.text: Divide or stick together?

explanation.surface: A question of whether to split up or stay united.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb has two opposite senses: to split with a blade, and (archaic) to cling faithfully to someone.

clue.text: I try a well-planned permutation-it comes up on the pools

definitions.text: it comes up on the pools

indicators.note: a permutation is a rearrangement, here a deliberately planned one, so the preceding letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A football-pools punter tries a carefully worked-out permutation of their forecasts.
explanation.walkthrough: The football pools were a British betting game where punters entered 'perms' of results; here the pools are ponds. 'planned permutation' rearranges I TRY A WELL.
explanation.definitionFit: This aquatic flower rises from the bottom of ponds to bloom on the surface.

clue.text: English fleet that is lucky for some

parts.note: RN, the Royal Navy, is Britain's fleet
i.e. (id est) is the abbreviation for 'that is'

explanation.surface: A naval tribute: the English fleet has brought good fortune to some.
explanation.walkthrough: ERNIE is the machine that picks winning numbers for British Premium Bonds, a state savings lottery, so it is lucky only for the winners.
explanation.definitionFit: The random-number generator behind Premium Bond prize draws brings winnings to a fortunate few holders.

clue.text: Hide article about king? Just the opposite

indicators.note: one piece placed about another means it goes round it
reverses the stated arrangement, so the king goes round the article instead of the article round the king

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's legendary king
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Instructions to wrap an item round a monarch, then a reversal of the order.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, 'article about king' puts the king inside; 'Just the opposite' flips which piece contains which, and 'Hide' is a noun, an animal skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A hide is an animal skin, which once tanned becomes this material.

clue.text: Hide pictures of military display

explanation.surface: Concealing the images from an army parade.
explanation.definitionFit: Inked designs on skin are one sense; an evening show of drumming and marching bands, as at Edinburgh, is the other.

clue.text: Air T-shirt badly and you could get this condition

indicators.note: done badly, the letters of the shirt phrase are put in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: Airing a T-shirt carelessly might leave you with some ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges the nine letters of AIR T-SHIRT.
explanation.definitionFit: Joint inflammation causing pain and stiffness is a medical condition.

clue.text: Cheeky drops in rents

explanation.surface: Cheeky reductions in what tenants pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Drops running down the cheeks are weeping; rips in fabric are the other sense, pronounced differently.

clue.text: Old-fashioned assembly in shed

parts.note: something no longer in fashion is out
a legislative assembly is a house, such as the House of Commons

explanation.surface: An antiquated parliamentary gathering held in a garden shed.
explanation.definitionFit: A small outbuilding standing apart from the main home is a shed.

clue.text: Red tongue of schoolboy, having swallowed last of strawberries

indicators.note: the schoolboy takes the following letter inside him, as if eating it

parts.note: an Etonian is a pupil at Eton College

indicators.note: points to the final letter of the fruit's name

explanation.surface: A schoolboy's tongue turned red after eating strawberries.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is an elite English boarding school. 'Red' means Soviet: Estonia was part of the USSR, so its language was a 'Red tongue'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Finnic language of a former Soviet Baltic republic is a communist-era tongue.

clue.text: Artist in trouble — here's a fine kettle of fish

definitions.text: here's a fine kettle of fish

indicators.note: a word in trouble is disordered, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A painter in difficulties exclaims at the mess they are in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' looks like part of the definition but rearranges ARTIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in dire straits is a predicament, and 'a fine kettle of fish' is an idiom for a mess.

clue.text: How this early composer travelled?

parts.note: the Tudor composer's name read as two words describes a way of travelling: via highway, abbreviated as on a map

explanation.surface: A music historian wonders about a Renaissance musician's journeys.
explanation.walkthrough: William Byrd was an English Tudor composer; split his name as BY RD, using the map abbreviation RD for road.
explanation.definitionFit: William Byrd wrote church music in sixteenth-century England, so he is an early composer.

clue.text: Overgenerous section of margin

indicators.note: a section is a part of a longer word, so the letters are found inside it

explanation.surface: Part of a profit margin is too generous.
explanation.definitionFit: An edge or border, such as a grass strip beside a road, is a margin.

clue.text: Country dance very fast, voila!

parts.note: the hey (or hay) is an old country dance with interweaving figures
presto is the musical direction for a very fast tempo

explanation.surface: A rapid folk dance finishes with a flourish.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjuror's exclamation when revealing a trick is the same as 'there you are!'

clue.text: Doctor in row makes deal, say

indicators.note: the doctor's letters are placed inside the row

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor in an argument strikes a bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deal' is not a bargain but a type of soft pine or fir wood; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Deal is sawn softwood, an example of wood used for building.

clue.text: Shots from Norwich City, for example

explanation.surface: Goal attempts by a football club.
explanation.walkthrough: Norwich City is a football club in Norfolk, home of the Broads, a network of rivers and lakes; a team is a side.
explanation.definitionFit: A volley from all a ship's guns on one flank is one sense; a team (side) from the Norfolk Broads area is the other.

clue.text: Particulars of a listed building?

parts.note: in Britain a listed building is protected for its history, and the specific features that earn the listing are its particulars

explanation.surface: An estate agent's brochure for a historic property.
explanation.walkthrough: A listed building is one on Britain's register of protected historic structures; the clue asks for its particulars, which also suggests an itemised list.
explanation.definitionFit: Individual facts or features recorded about something are its particulars.

clue.text: Sewing mailbags for this assisted crime?

definitions.text: Sewing mailbags for this assisted crime?

parts.words: Sewing mailbags for this assisted crime?
parts.note: sewing mailbags was the traditional prison chore, work done behind bars, and a crime helped by someone on the staff has the same name

explanation.surface: A convict's prison labour turns out to have been an accomplice's crime.
explanation.walkthrough: Sewing mailbags was a traditional British prison task, a job done while locked in.
explanation.definitionFit: A robbery aided by an employee of the target is described as committed with help from within.

clue.text: Promotes benefits

explanation.surface: Furthers perks for staff.
explanation.definitionFit: To move forward someone's cause is to further it; loans paid ahead of time are the other sense.

clue.text: Light play where patients sit

parts.note: daylight, so light means day
room to move is play, as in a loose rope

explanation.surface: A light-hearted drama staged on a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: A communal lounge in a hospital is the place patients relax during the daytime.

clue.text: First of March and everyone on way to palace?

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of the month's name

parts.note: everyone means all

explanation.surface: On the first of March, everyone heads down the road to the palace.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mall is the London avenue leading to Buckingham Palace.
explanation.definitionFit: The ceremonial avenue in London runs up to Buckingham Palace, so it is the royal route.

clue.text: Cruel treatment of male issue, possibly

indicators.note: signals that the word may appear in another arrangement

explanation.surface: A male child might be the victim of cruelty.
explanation.definitionFit: Treating someone harshly or wrongly is abuse.

clue.text: Single girl, one assigned to embassy

parts.note: Miss is the title of an unmarried woman
I is the Roman numeral for one
someone on a team or rota is assigned to it

explanation.surface: An unmarried woman is posted to a diplomatic office.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomatic delegation sent abroad is a mission.

clue.text: Stage award

explanation.surface: A theatre prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A step or level in a process is one sense; a university qualification conferred on graduates is the other.

clue.text: Terriers from dealer, as I ordered

indicators.note: ordered letters are rearranged into a new sequence

explanation.surface: A buyer gets dogs from a breeder, as requested.
explanation.definitionFit: These large rough-coated dogs from Yorkshire are a breed of terrier.

clue.text: Daring restoration, for example

parts.note: Daring is the name of a Royal Navy warship, and repair work carried out on such a vessel in dock is the kind of restoration meant

explanation.surface: A bold renovation of an old house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daring' looks like an adjective, but HMS Daring is a Royal Navy destroyer; a ship's overhaul is the restoration.
explanation.definitionFit: Overhauling and re-equipping a vessel is a restoration of it.

clue.text: Hospital border as windbreak

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital
an edge is a border

explanation.surface: A hospital's boundary planting shelters it from the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A row of dense shrubs planted to shelter a field breaks the wind.

clue.text: Two symbols, we hear, of a supercilious sort?

indicators.note: signals that the piece is heard spoken and spelt another way

parts.note: a high-hat is a snob, someone who looks down on others

explanation.surface: Two signs seem to describe a snobbish person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'symbols' is heard as cymbals: a drum kit's pair of cymbals on a pedal stand. 'we hear' also turns HIGH-HAT, a snob, into the drum term.
explanation.definitionFit: The pedal-operated pair of clashing plates on a drum kit is two cymbals.

clue.text: Snuff-box?

parts.note: to snuff it is slang for to die, so the box goes with dying rather than with tobacco

explanation.surface: A container for powdered tobacco.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snuff it' is British slang for die, so the box is for someone who has snuffed it.
explanation.definitionFit: The box a dead person is buried in goes with snuffing it.

clue.text: Goatsucker gets nasty shock after dark

indicators.note: the shock is placed after the dark, in the order the clue states

parts.note: after dark means at night
a jar is a jolt or unpleasant shock

explanation.surface: A goat-thief gets a fright after nightfall.
explanation.walkthrough: Goatsucker is an old name for this bird, which was believed to suck milk from goats.
explanation.definitionFit: A nocturnal insect-eating bird was once believed to steal milk from goats.

clue.text: Easy shot of a photographer's model

explanation.surface: An easy picture of a photographer's model.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy catch or chance is one sense; a person who poses for a portrait is the other.

clue.text: Temperamental daughter leaves old English composer

indicators.note: the daughter leaves, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: John Dunstable was a fifteenth-century English composer

explanation.surface: A moody girl walks out on an elderly musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone volatile and prone to mood swings is temperamental.
